ua-0TmA.title: Houses: tidy single-storey, orange or diamond roofs
ua-0TmA.summary: Villages are fairly linear and organised, with single-storey houses close to the street. Roofs are orange tile or diamond-shaped slate, like Hungary, Czechia and Slovakia.

ua-3Khl.title: Pole: wooden with concrete base blocks
ua-3Khl.summary: Wooden poles also occur, sometimes with concrete support blocks at the base.

ua-7Sho.title: Landscape: hilly, forested, curvy roads
ua-7Sho.summary: In the west, a much hillier, sometimes mountainous area, heavily forested with many pines and little farming. Roads are curvy rather than straight highways.

ua-7ytl.title: Bus stop: yellow-green with sunflowers
ua-7ytl.summary: Bus shelters painted bright yellow and green with sunflowers and a local brand name, Оліс, in the south.

ua-9V71.title: Guardrail: painted black and white
ua-9V71.summary: Guardrails and barriers are often painted black and white, like Russia.

ua-9fKw.title: Road: potholes, cracks, warped pavement
ua-9fKw.summary: Some of the worst roads in Europe: most rural roads are full of potholes, cracks and warped asphalt. Helps against Russia, which has somewhat better roads.

differs.how: Russian roads are generally somewhat better

ua-AXOh.title: Pole: square concrete, varied tops
ua-AXOh.summary: Mostly square concrete poles with various tops and sometimes white paint at the bottom. Russia and Lithuania have similar ones.

ua-AkYz.title: Language: Russian in east and south, Ы and Э
ua-AkYz.summary: Russian appears in the east and south. The letters Ы and Э are Russian only. Street is улица (ул.) and city is город (г.).

differs.how: Russia uses Ы, Э, улица, город everywhere

ua-CdRn.title: Objects: painted blue and yellow
ua-CdRn.summary: Random roadside objects, most often fences, are painted blue and yellow like the flag.

ua-G7CF.title: Coverage: almost all summer
ua-G7CF.summary: Nearly all coverage is from summer: green leaves, people in summer clothes. Five big cities have autumn coverage with fall colours and colder weather.

ua-Hkd1.title: Plants: tall poplar trees
ua-Hkd1.summary: Tall poplars are common in many parts of the country. Some parts of Russia have them, but most of Russia does not.

differs.how: Most of Russia lacks tall poplars

ua-IG9J.title: Google car: a leaf visible on the back
ua-IG9J.summary: A leaf is visible on the back of the Google car on several roads in the west, around Ternopil, Brody, Dubno and Pochaiv.

ua-INTC.title: Landscape: warmer, drier, fewer forests
ua-INTC.summary: Towards the south it gets warmer and drier, with fewer forests and more shrubs and open fields. The change is subtle but noticeable with practice.

ua-J6ak.title: Houses: grey Soviet apartment blocks
ua-J6ak.summary: Big Soviet-era blocks of light grey brick or stacked concrete panels, usually rundown. Russian cities have the same. The Baltic states have them too, but better kept.

ua-JmjH.title: Google car: rare black, white or grey cars
ua-JmjH.summary: Rarely, other cars show up: black or white with a long antenna, or grey with a short antenna. These also exist in several other countries, including Russia.

ua-MArz.title: Language: 'вулиця' means street
ua-MArz.summary: Street is вулиця, short вул. In Russian it is улица, short ул., with no в at the start.

ua-NPC1.title: Signs: lots of Hungarian text
ua-NPC1.summary: Near the Hungarian border most people are Hungarian, so many signs are in Hungarian, bilingual or even only Hungarian.

ua-QxHe.title: Pole: red band across
ua-QxHe.summary: Poles with a red band across them are unique to one mining city.

ua-TCLY.title: Coverage: five cities from 2011, autumn
ua-TCLY.summary: Five major cities were covered in 2011 in autumn, with fall colours and people in cold-weather clothes. Most of it was overwritten by newer summer coverage in three cities, but it remains in the other two, one of which has no newer coverage at all.

ua-VZe4.title: Plate: first two letters show the region
ua-VZe4.summary: The first two letters on blue-and-yellow-strip plates give the registration region, which is handy if the plate is not blurred. The codes are not intuitive, so you must learn them. Older plates use number codes like Russia.

ua-Vcd1.title: Google car: silver car, short antenna
ua-Vcd1.summary: The old 2011 coverage in one southern port city used a silver car with a short antenna, not a black or white one with a long antenna. It may be fully blurred.

ua-Wve0.title: Bollard: red reflector wrapping all round
ua-Wve0.summary: White post with a red band and reflector that wraps around it, in the far west. It is identical to the standard Polish bollard.

ua-YsNh.title: Houses: brick houses behind fences, dirt roads
ua-YsNh.summary: Suburbs and small towns have brick houses, often with corrugated roofs and always behind fences. They look rundown and overgrown, and most roads are unpaved.

ua-a4Vs.title: Google car: yellow Opel flag on antenna
ua-a4Vs.summary: On one side of the road to the exclusion zone, a yellow flag with an Opel logo flies from the car's antenna.

ua-aOBs.title: Plate: long white, blue-yellow strip
ua-aOBs.summary: Long white plates with a blue and yellow strip on the left, the flag colours. Older plates have a strip where the colours are hard to see. Russian plates are all white without a strip.

differs.how: Russian plates are all white, no strip

ua-c205.title: Language: 'місто' means city
ua-c205.summary: City is місто, short м. Handy to tell it from other Cyrillic languages and to find the city name in an address.

ua-clFO.title: Plants: tall pines with orange-red bark
ua-clFO.summary: Scots pine forests, tall with orange-red bark, mostly in the north near the Belarus border, often mixed with broadleaf trees. The western mountains also have pines, but are hilly while the north is very flat.

ua-dZuO.title: Landscape: typical rural road, fields beyond trees
ua-dZuO.summary: Bad road, flat or gently rolling land, a line of trees or bushes with wide farm fields beyond, almost no buildings or traffic until the next town.

ua-ffx5.title: Sign: pedestrian sign, three stripes
ua-ffx5.summary: Pedestrian signs with three stripes. Russia, Estonia and Lithuania also use three stripes.

ua-fmwm.title: Coverage: trekker to an abandoned town
ua-fmwm.summary: A special trekker covers a road to an abandoned town in an exclusion zone. Most of the road looks normal, but in the town you see completely abandoned, overgrown buildings that look eerie.

ua-ftY0.title: Pole: diagonal support beams
ua-ftY0.summary: Poles often have diagonal support beams.

ua-iXrj.title: Chevron: red with white arrows
ua-iXrj.summary: Red chevrons with white arrows. Russia and Estonia use exactly the same.

ua-lm-2985.title: Sign: three-stripe pedestrian figure, slimmer
ua-lm-2985.summary: Of the three-stripe pedestrian signs, Estonia has a detailed figure and Russia yellow borders. Lithuania's figure is a bit fatter in the torso, with a more vibrant blue.

differs.how: Lithuania's figure is fatter, with more vibrant blue

ua-lm-740283.title: Street sign: castle logo on the left
ua-lm-740283.summary: A street sign with a castle logo on its left confirms the big western city. That city also has unique cobblestone streets, found elsewhere only in a few small far-western towns.

ua-lm-740289.title: Street sign: blue, white line, Latin lower line
ua-lm-740289.summary: Blue signs with a white line in the middle: top text in Cyrillic, bottom text in Latin letters. House numbers use the same design.

ua-lm-740324.title: Houses: many tall buildings
ua-lm-740324.summary: If you know it's the country and see many large, tall buildings, it is most likely the capital.

ua-nLtW.title: Domain: region codes like .te.ua
ua-nLtW.summary: Regional second-level web domains sometimes appear, such as .te.ua. Mostly intuitive from the region name.

ua-p0kA.title: Coverage: unique visual glitch, one western city
ua-p0kA.summary: A particular visual glitch, shown in the image, appears only in one western city within the country.

ua-pjlN.title: Google car: black or white car, long antenna
ua-pjlN.summary: The old 2011 coverage used a black car in one eastern city (no newer coverage there, so a red car is never there) and a white car, now rare, in three other cities. Both have a long antenna.

ua-rOmV.title: Soil: red dirt with Brazilian-style poles
ua-rOmV.summary: Around an iron mine, dirt tracks have red soil and Brazilian-style poles, which makes it good bait. The plants are far less tropical, and the car has a long antenna.

differs.how: Less tropical plants, and a long antenna on the car

ua-sSrn.title: Language: Cyrillic with Є, Ґ, І, Ї
ua-sSrn.summary: Cyrillic script with the letters Є, Ґ, І and Ї, which Russian does not use. Don't mix Є up with Э, which is Russian and Belarusian.

differs.how: Russian has no Є, Ґ, І or Ї

ua-t7jl.title: Coverage: May look, yellowish leaves
ua-t7jl.summary: May coverage is mostly in the western half. Look for a yellowish tint on otherwise green leaves. June and July coverage also appears there and elsewhere.

ua-tc2U.title: Coverage: gaps in the south-east and south
ua-tc2U.summary: Most coverage between cities is on main roads. There is almost none in the south-east except one city, and none south of the port city near Romania.

differs.how: Romania has coverage there, this country has none

ua-uPIf.title: Phone numbers: 2-digit area code per region
ua-uPIf.summary: Landlines start with a 2-digit area code, one per region. A third digit of 2 means the region's capital. Mobiles start with 50, 63, 66-68, 73 or 91-99 and say nothing about location.

ua-ugIv.title: Google car: red Gen 3 car
ua-ugIv.summary: All coverage is Gen 3, mostly with a red car that sometimes has an antenna and sometimes not. The car is not always visible. Russia never has the red car and often has Gen 4.

differs.how: Russia has no red car, and may have Gen 4 or Gen 2

ua-wdxm.title: Coverage: cities, main roads, rural tracks
ua-wdxm.summary: Coverage is mostly cities and the main roads between them. Quite common exception: very rural tracks right next to cities.

ua-wjAJ.title: Plants: blooming sunflower fields, south and east
ua-wjAJ.summary: Sunflowers only bloom from late July, so blooming fields mostly show in the far south and east. Fields not yet in bloom exist almost everywhere and look like normal crops.
